title: Automorphism tensor comparison on arbitrary quotient-semilinear systems
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible and $g:S\to S$ an automorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_n=(A_n)_S$, $\rho_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$, and $\widehat R_S=\lim_n B_n$, with projections $\pi_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $F=g^{-1}$ and $c_n:FB_n\xrightarrow{\sim}B_n$, $c_{\widehat R}:F\widehat R_S\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat R_S$ for the canonical coefficient isomorphisms [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. On $FM$ transport the $B_n$ action by $c_n^{-1}$. Let $\mathscr S_S$ be the abelian category of strict $B_n$-module systems, whose maps $v_n:M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{\rho_n}M_n$ are quotient-linear and whose kernels and cokernels are componentwise [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use ordinary unbounded complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

For every such system complex $M$, the termwise comparison
$$j_{n,M}:FM_n\longrightarrow T_nM_n:=FM_n\otimes_{FB_n}B_n,\qquad x\longmapsto x\otimes1$$
is an isomorphism of complexes of $B_n$-module sheaves, natural in $M_n$, with inverse on local tensor generators $x\otimes a\mapsto c_n^{-1}(a)x$. The maps on local generators
$$\tau_n:T_{n+1}M_{n+1}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{\rho_n}T_nM_n,\qquad x\otimes a\longmapsto F(v_n)(x)\otimes\rho_n(a)$$
define quotient-linear transitions and satisfy
$$\tau_nj_{n+1,M}=j_{n,M}F(v_n),\qquad x\otimes1\longmapsto F(v_n)(x)\otimes\rho_n(1)=F(v_n)(x)\otimes1.$$
These isomorphisms and transitions commute with differentials and all system chain maps. They remain linear after restriction through the completed coefficient projections, with the actual squares
$$\rho_nc_{n+1}=c_nF(\rho_n),\qquad \pi_nc_{\widehat R}=c_nF(\pi_n).$$
Thus $j$ is a natural isomorphism between the levelwise inverse-image and tensor-pullback functors on strict system complexes. The underlying module-system functor $G:M\mapsto(FM_n,Fv_n)_n$ is exact. No flatness, cartesianness, boundedness or finite Tor-amplitude condition on $M$ is required.

proof.text: Construction laws in Lean: continuity of the product site transport follows by restricting to every vertical slice and applying pro-etale postcomposition continuity. The coefficient morphism is an isomorphism because its components become the recorded invertible finite coefficient maps after forgetting commutativity; both forgetting functors reflect isomorphisms. The scalar-extension identity and composition laws specialize the existing scalarExtension_map_id and scalarExtension_map_comp. Inverse-image additivity is sectionwise. Tensor additivity follows sectionwise from the extension/restriction adjunction and then from additivity of module sheafification. These construction laws do not replace any of the seven comparison steps below. Raw continuous module transport uses PresheafOfModules.pushforward₀ directly, with continuity supplying its sheaf condition. Its exactness is proved with abstract ring sheaves before specializing to the coefficient system, keeping concrete coefficient constructions folded.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (3), the maps $c_n:FB_n\to B_n$ are ring-sheaf isomorphisms. Apply its ring-homomorphism naturality to $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ to get $\rho_nc_{n+1}=c_nF(\rho_n)$. The completed structure isomorphism of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] is defined by its components, so $\pi_nc_{\widehat R}=c_nF(\pi_n)$. This gives the actual two coefficient squares in the statement, not merely abstract identifications of coefficient objects. The limit projections of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] also satisfy $\pi_n=\rho_n\pi_{n+1}$ by the defining cone equation. Inverting the $c$'s in these squares gives $F(\rho_n)c_{n+1}^{-1}=c_n^{-1}\rho_n$ and $F(\pi_n)c_{\widehat R}^{-1}=c_n^{-1}\pi_n$. Lean implementation: apply the coefficient-component naturality theorem to the adjacent horizontal arrow and identify the sequence-ring restriction with the actual quotient transition. The completed square is limit.lift_π for the recorded inverseImageCompletedCoefficientMap.

proof.text: Fix a degree $q$ and level $n$. The inverse-image construction [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] gives $FM_n^q$ its $FB_n$-module structure. Apply [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso] with ring sheaves $R'=FB_n$, $S'=B_n$, $c=c_n$, and module $FM_n^q$. Its target is exactly the transported action in the item, and its inverse is $j_n^q:x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Its forward map $\theta_n^q=(j_n^q)^{-1}$ sends a local tensor $x\otimes a$ to $c_n^{-1}(a)x$. Here a local tensor denotes its image under the presheaf-to-sheafification unit, exactly as in that lemma. Naturality of that lemma applied to $F(d^q)$ gives $(F(d^q)\otimes1)j_n^q=j_n^{q+1}F(d^q)$. Thus the $j_n^q$ and their inverses are chain maps and give the required natural isomorphism $j_{n,M}:FM_n\cong T_nM_n$. Lean implementation: apply exists_scalarExtensionRingIso directly on the vertical sequence site to the system coefficient isomorphism and the raw module system. This assembles every finite-level comparison at once. Its target is raw site transport followed by scalar restriction through the inverse coefficient map. The inverse coefficient component is identified with c_n inverse by uniqueness of inverses.

proof.text:
Write $w_n=F(v_n)$. Applying inverse image to the action equation for the quotient-linear map $v_n$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] gives $w_n(rx)=F(\rho_n)(r)w_n(x)$ for local $r\in FB_{n+1}$. For $a\in B_{n+1}$, the first inverted coefficient square of Step 1 therefore gives
$$w_n(c_{n+1}^{-1}(a)x)=F(\rho_n)(c_{n+1}^{-1}(a))w_n(x)=c_n^{-1}(\rho_n(a))w_n(x).$$
This is precisely $B_{n+1}$-linearity into the restriction along $\rho_n$ of the transported $B_n$-module [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Hence the unchanged underlying maps $w_n$ define strict quotient-linear system transitions. Identities, composites and the system-morphism equations are preserved by the functor $F$, so this constructs the functor $G$ on module systems.

proof.text:
Define the sheaf map $\tau_n=j_{n,M}\,w_n\,\theta_{n+1}$, restricting the target scalars along $\rho_n$. It is quotient-linear by Step 3 and the $B_n$-linear isomorphisms of Step 2. The normalized inverse formula of [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso] gives, on every local tensor,
$$\tau_n(x\otimes a)=j_nw_n(c_{n+1}^{-1}(a)x)=j_n(c_n^{-1}(\rho_n(a))w_n(x))=w_n(x)\otimes\rho_n(a).$$
Thus it has exactly the proposed formula and is a globally defined sheaf morphism; its definition needs no assumption that a section of a sheafified tensor is globally pure. In particular $\tau_nj_{n+1}=j_nw_n$, since $\theta_{n+1}j_{n+1}=1$, and on $x$ this reads $w_n(x)\otimes\rho_n(1)=w_n(x)\otimes1$. In the sequence-site implementation the tensor object already has restriction maps. scalarExtensionSection_naturality proves their displayed local-generator formula, and naturality of the comparison sheaf morphism proves the tensor-unit transition square. Hence these restrictions agree with the conjugated transition just described.

proof.text:
The maps $w_n$ commute with differentials because $v_n$ are transitions of a system complex. The $j_n$ and $\theta_n$ are chain maps by Step 2, so their composite defining $\tau_n$ is a chain map. For a system chain map $h:M\to N$, put $h'_n=F(h_n)$ and $h^T_n=F(h_n)\otimes1$. Naturality in Step 2 gives $h^T_nj_{n,M}=j_{n,N}h'_n$ and $\theta_{n,N}h^T_n=h'_n\theta_{n,M}$. Consequently
$$h^T_n\tau_{n,M}=j_{n,N}h'_nw_{n,M}\theta_{n+1,M}=j_{n,N}w_{n,N}h'_{n+1}\theta_{n+1,M}=\tau_{n,N}h^T_{n+1}.$$
The middle equality is the image under $F$ of the system-morphism equation for $h$. These equalities prove that $j$ is a natural isomorphism on strict system complexes, in the ordinary sense of chain maps of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Transitions over several levels are composites of the adjacent ones; cancellation of $\theta_kj_k$ proves the same compatibility for them. Lean implementation: NatIso.ofComponents assembles the natural scalar-extension comparisons on module systems; NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex then gives the natural isomorphism on ordinary unbounded cochain complexes.

proof.text: The completed coefficient square of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], inverted as in Step 1, says $F(\pi_n)(c_{\widehat R}^{-1}(b))=c_n^{-1}(\pi_n(b))$ for each local completed scalar $b$. Hence the action on $FM_n$ obtained by first restricting $M_n$ along $\pi_n$, applying $F$, and transporting along $c_{\widehat R}$ is exactly its transported $B_n$-action restricted along $\pi_n$: both act by $c_n^{-1}(\pi_n(b))$. Thus $j_n$ and $\theta_n$, already $B_n$-linear, are linear for these actual completed actions [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Moreover, the cone equation $\rho_n\pi_{n+1}=\pi_n$ of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and quotient-linearity give $\tau_n(\pi_{n+1}(b)z)=\pi_n(b)\tau_n(z)$; the identical calculation with $w_n$ proves its completed linearity. All squares established above therefore remain squares of completed-module maps, with the specified coefficient projections. Lean implementation: apply map_smul to the comparison at (n,U) with the scalar π_n(b), and identify its transported action with c_n inverse(π_n(b)). The completed coefficient square is proved independently as in Step 1.

proof.text: The strict system category is the recorded category of module sheaves on the vertical sequence site [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Form the product of the identity equivalence on the natural-number index category with the pro-etale site equivalence [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Continuous pushforward and its inverse give an equivalence H on abelian sheaves on this sequence site. Forgetting the transported coefficient action of the inverse-system functor G gives H: at each (n,U), both underlying groups and underlying maps are those of M at (n,gU). The identity maps on these groups give the comparison after forgetting coefficients. The forgetful functor from module sheaves to abelian sheaves preserves finite limits and colimits and reflects them [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Therefore G preserves finite limits and colimits and is exact. This implements inverse-image exactness on the entire sequence site directly, avoiding a separate componentwise kernel/cokernel argument. All constructions are degreewise, with arbitrary module sheaves and arbitrary transitions; no flatness, cartesianness, boundedness or Tor-amplitude hypothesis is used.
